paragraphs: Envisio makes software for public agencies that need to turn a strategic plan into tracked work and reportable results. It is built for the public sector and, the company says, only the public sector. Customers span government, education, healthcare and nonprofit organizations.

Plans can be laid out as a cascade, a Gantt chart, tags or scorecards, depending on how the organization works. Staff get scheduled reminders to submit progress and performance updates. Those updates roll up automatically into reports covering actions, projects, measures and narrative. The same material feeds public dashboards a community can read. Every package includes unlimited users.

More than 200 organizations use Envisio, by the company's count. Example dashboards on the site include the City of Rockville's climate action plan, which tracks emissions reduction and renewable energy adoption. The company frames its purpose around a stated decline in trust in public institutions. It points to recognition as a GovTech 100 company. Chief executive Craig Ross was previously interim CEO at Euna Solutions and CEO of eCivis.

quote.text: Too often, those plans get stuck in spreadsheets, and nothing changes.
